failures.criterion: Acceptance 2: a red required check on the pull request's head resumes the implementer from testing, reviewing, retro, merging or awaiting_merge, except a red the tester planned.
failures.evidence: A push classified after its head arrived, which completes the carry of a code head's red to the handoff head that replaced it (classify.SettlementFor, carriedBack), sends the work back only in reviewing: workflow/pullrequest.go's push handler returns before standingRed when issue.Phase != phase.Reviewing (the guard that also gates reaskRound), so in testing, retro and merging the issue stays where it is with classify.HeadVerdict red for its head and no checks-red, no implementer start and no counted round. The implementer's own standingRed doc names a push classified late as one of the two non-CI facts that apply the rule, and no test had a row for it outside reviewing. Live path: the implementer's handoff push (implement.json) whose webhook reaches the daemon after the synchronize and after the implementer's completion moved the issue to testing, with the code head's red already recorded in implementing. Pinned by packages/daemon/internal/workflow/checks_red_test.go TestAPushClassifiedLateThatCompletesTheCarryOfARedSendsTheWorkBackFromEveryPhase (commit 881481d11a0e): LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:54332/postgres?sslmode=disable go -C packages/daemon test -count=1 ./internal/workflow -run TestAPushClassifiedLateThatCompletesTheCarryOfARedSendsTheWorkBackFromEveryPhase -v → --- FAIL testing (after the late push completed the carry the issue is in testing, want implementing), --- FAIL retro, --- FAIL merging, --- PASS reviewing. Applying standingRed before the reviewing guard (reaskRound stays reviewing's) in a scratch copy of the branch makes the test pass and leaves the whole workflow package green (go test ./internal/workflow -skip 'Consume|Captured|RateLimited|BackwardMoveNoRow|LateEventOfAnEarlier': ok, 82s); the implementer owns the fix.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 6: legion start --check-config refuses a file that still sets projects.<KEY>.review_workflows, and the daemon's boot refuses it too.
proof.surface: The legion CLI built from the branch at 9fb30a6c (go build -o /tmp/legion-bin ./cmd/legion) on four minimal legion.yaml files under /tmp/cfg (project LEGION, repo sjawhar/legion, state_dir, postgres_dsn, 0600 dispatch_token_file and operator_token_file, gates.design, both github_apps, nats_urls).
proof.command: /tmp/legion-bin start --check-config --config /tmp/cfg/rw.yaml (review_workflows: [.github/workflows/review.yml]); rw-empty.yaml (review_workflows: []); rw-null.yaml (review_workflows: with no value); rw-camel.yaml (reviewWorkflows: [...]); then timeout 20 /tmp/legion-bin start --config /tmp/cfg/rw.yaml
proof.observed: legion start: Unknown key "projects.LEGION.review_workflows" and exit 1 for rw, rw-empty and rw-null; legion start: Unknown key "projects.LEGION.reviewWorkflows" and exit 1 for rw-camel; the boot (legion start without --check-config) prints the same Unknown key line and exits 1 before any boot stage runs.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: a reviewer's APPROVE of the head ends the round whatever CI says at that commit, in the sequence this issue was filed for.
proof.surface: The daemon's workflow engine on the embedded Postgres, driven through intake.ApplyFact with the facts in production order (a throwaway probe test, not committed).
proof.command: Seed reviewing with code head green on lint, typecheck, test, pr-title; apply pushedFromTo(code, review1, .legion/LEGION-208/review.json, legion-reviewer[bot]), syncedTo(review1), the approval of review1, a PullRequestChecks at review1 with CheckRuns [pr-title] and Failing [] (the review event's run, replacing the carried green with no verdict), in both orders, then the reviewer's HandoffComplete.
proof.observed: The issue is in retro after the completion in both orders; notices carry no checks-red and no review-stuck. A second probe: the approval, then a red settlement at the head before the completion, moves the issue to implementing with the implementer's start waiting on the reviewer and the late completion refused HANDOFF_NOT_CURRENT_PHASE; a third: a hold retry (completion, ClaimFailed, approval, red, RetryOrEscalate retry) ends in implementing with a checks-red, as the implementer's deviation says.
proof.negativeControl: The same TestAnApprovalEndsTheRoundWhateverCISays red and undecided rows fail on main e4ec5a20 with HANDOFF_NOT_CURRENT_PHASE on the half after the red sent the work back, and TestARoundNoReviewDecidesTellsTheArchitect (a COMMENT-only round) still passes on the branch, so the surviving stuck cause is intact.

risks: D2's daemon side (probe, not pinned): after a red moves retro to implementing, an implementer completion reporting any commit but its last handoff is accepted as the implementation's and moves the issue to testing; HANDOFF_NOT_NEW catches only the last handoff commit. The refusal of a retro completion rests on pi-legion's lookup of implement.json at the state's phase, read before the commit is found and the completion posted, so a red landing inside that window lets a retro completion through. Narrow; recorded for the architect, no change asked.

A red standing when a phase is entered is not re-read (plan D4): an implementer that completes on a code head already red, its handoff push and synchronize known, hands the tester a head whose verdict is red with nothing to act on it until the next CI fact or READY. Accepted by the plan; noted because the failure above is the neighbouring case where the daemon learns of the red after entry.
